title: introduce-multi-model-hotpath-simulator-and-cliff-edge-reporter
author: Evelyn Park
description:
Motivation: We've observed production tail events that only emerge when heterogeneous models are exercised together (e.g., a heavy LLM rerank paired with a small chat model). Existing single-model workload runners miss cross-model interference on shared GPU resources and scheduling-induced cliff edges. This PR adds a Multi-Model Hotpath Simulator (MMHS) and a Cliff-Edge Reporter pipeline to capture those behaviors and produce deterministic, analyzable artifacts.

What this PR contains: 
- MMHS: a workload runner that can orchestrate concurrent request streams across multiple model types with configurable sequence distributions, KV primer policies, and controlled priming overlap windows. It supports both synchronous and streaming patterns to reproduce mixed RPC behavior.
- PULSE smoothing: latency post-processor that applies phase-aware smoothing (PULSE algorithm) to reduce noise while preserving transient cliff events for detection.
- Cliff-Edge Reporter: a reporting pipeline that identifies stepwise throughput/latency cliffs, annotates affected kernels, and emits an HTML+JSON artifact for triage.
- Integration hooks: small adapters to the existing bench harness to allow scheduling MMHS runs in nightly pipelines and to attach tapes for deterministic replays.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implement multi-model runner and orchestration primitives
- [x] Add PULSE smoothing component and CLI flag to toggle smoothing
- [x] Add reporter pipeline + artifact writer (HTML summary + compact JSON)
- [x] Unit tests for scheduler, primer, and reporter edge-cases
- [x] End-to-end smoke run in CI with a 3-model mix

How to run locally: 
- python -m benchlab.runner --config examples/multi_model_mix.yaml --out artifacts/run-<timestamp>
- artifacts contain run.trace (binary), run-summary.json, and report.html generated by the Cliff-Edge Reporter.

Expected outcomes and measured results from internal CI run: 
- 3-model nightly mix (chat-small, rerank-medium, large-gen) reproduced a 2.8x p99 latency spike when KV primer overlap was 30-50ms.
- PULSE smoothing retained the cliff event while reducing per-minute noise by ~22% enabling more stable cliff detection thresholds.

Related items: Linear ENG-4721 (benchmark design), ENG-4882 (reporting UX). References to prior investigations: incident INT-1024 spike analysis.

Notes on safety and reproducibility: The runner supports a deterministic 'tape' mode that records request timing jitter and can replay with recorded seeds to reproduce cliffs. The artifacts include provenance fields for exact binary hashes and kernel versions.

release_notes: Add multi-model hotpath simulator and cliff-edge reporter to benchmark-lab. Enables detection of cross-model interference and stepwise latency cliffs; includes PULSE smoothing and deterministic tape replay mode for reproducibility.
notes_for_oncall: If nightly runs begin producing frequent cliff artifacts after rollout, reduce concurrency in multi-model mixes or enable PULSE smoothing until root cause is found. Artifacts are written to s3://benchlab-artifacts/<run-id> with provenance.
